new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened from the MIRROR and read all 10 page images (no text layer; no scanned run). Title/identity: folio 1 header reads 'SURVEY word LIST (STANDARD) LANGUAGE HAHON (Banaia) VILLAGE (OR AREA) Lalum DATE 23 March, 1963.. Taken at TSIMBA Mission.. INFORMANT Joseph Vamas AGE 22 SEX Male RELIABILITY Good', handwritten 'This list is found on Tape #3' and 'Bougainville Survey Extra' = PARADISEC AC2-NSBHAH101, i.e. the Capell AC2 Hahon fieldnote item named in the first half of the citation (same_work_ok for that half; the Capell 1971 CTL 8 chapter remains unobtained, correctly reported as De Gruyter paywall / not on archive.org). Quote check item by item against the images: 1 'obno?, 2 pats'no?…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. This is primary DATA (a stress-marked 1963 survey word list), not a rule statement: it supplies the first stress evidence held by the project for Hahon (predominantly penultimate marks, with a final-stressed minority), to be weighed by a reviewer; no catalog record or earlier statement exists to agree or conflict with.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement about stress anywhere (it is a bare elicitation word list, no notes or prose). Capell marks primary stress with a raised stroke before the stressed syllable on almost every response. Tallying the ~170 marked forms: the mark falls on the PENULTIMATE syllable in the clear majority of citation forms (ma'tano?, nao'bana, toi'sona, poo'tana, pa'tamba, 'bika, 'kuso, i'ana, 'pauna, tsu'numbu, ka'kato, ku'kana, 'tana, tau'nima, 'sabun..); a sizeable minority is FINAL-stressed, notably several 3sg-possessed body-part nouns in -no? (pats'no?, pana'no?, is'no?, koma'no? beside penult ma'tano?, be'nano?) and consonant-final words (bom'bon, uu'pas, too'bus, ro'mbon), plus a few vowel-final ones (totsun'na, toanan'na, kao'bo, sinia'ba); a few forms carry the mark earlier ('saanana, keta'panano?, and inflected verb forms with the mark on the root: oyato'bakato?, oyato'bantono, tsuratoa'tatena). So the data show predominantly penultimate stress with unexplained final-stress items; no single fixed position can be asserted from this source and the source itself asserts none.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated. Two marks appear only on reduplicated/long forms ('para'para 'moon', item 33; tsu'numbuka'tinao 'the man will go tomorrow', item 179).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated (data only); see rule_in_words for the final-stressed and root-stressed items observed.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell 1963: Hahon ('Banaia' per the header), Lalum village, recorded at Tsimba Mission, NW Bougainville; informant born at Porapora, raised at Lalum ('He has forgotten his old Porapora dialect now'). Logan dk0305: three Hahon dialects (Aravia; Savon/Benmat/Puto; Petspets/Doaso) plus Ratsua, now treated as a separate language (rats1237).

sources.note: Landing page contents list (verbatim items): 'for 25% of the recordings, detailed phonetic, phonological and morphological annotations'; 'Hahon-English/English-Hahon dictionary'; 'PhD thesis on grammar and dialectology in Hahon'; 'conference presentations and journal articles'. The visible item list (24 bundles) contains only recordings, transcriptions, life histories, dialect surveys and a 'Depositor's Metadata' bundle; no grammar, thesis or phonology document could be opened. Nothing about stress is visible.

sources.note: Nothing for Hahon. Chapter 7 (North-West Solomonic) gives Hahon only in consonant-correspondence tables (pp. 219-222) and lexical reflexes; data source for Hahon is listed as 'SIL' (p. 409); fn. 78 (p. 421) says Hahon retains final a and o but loses final i and u. All 'stress' hits in the book concern Ali/Schouten languages (pp. ~118-119), not Bougainville.
